_slice.why: S2's spec block is a whole page, so it carries about ninety card-internal rules that belong to S2b. DROPPED is enforced for this spec only once S2b is actually in the tree.

facts.means: the card sheet is APPLIED, by whichever of the two files imports it. Not 'the file exists': it was committed inert first so the transcription could be reviewed before it could move a pixel. The second spelling is the one that shipped - S2b's import landed in Shell.tsx, not page.tsx, and the single-file version of this fact read false on the very tree it exists to detect.
the page renders the shell, which is what makes the shell's import reach THIS page. Without it the branch above would accept a sheet imported by a shell nobody renders.

the markup the sheet styles is really rendering. The snapshot's own card is a stack of div.phase[data-phase] and the transcription keeps the attribute, so this is design-anchored rather than invented.

.mascot-riso.why: The owner's 19:40Z ruling says the mascot follows its column. The frozen snapshot does NOT carry the !important width/max-width/height that the ruling describes - grep finds none on that rule - so the ruling's intent is transcribed here and the discrepancy between the ruling's words and the snapshot is recorded in the PR body rather than silently resolved either way.

.tag.why: RE-SCOPED TO OUTRANK globals.css, SAME DECLARATIONS (#575). The legacy sheet styles the same element at the same specificity, so the design's own selector loses on source order alone. One ancestor is added - `html` for element rules, `.stage` for page furniture - which raises specificity without changing what is painted. The spec's key and ours therefore differ while the CSS does not, which the checker reports as one dropped rule plus one added rule: the same divergence twice. Under the spec's own key we now ship nothing: this is the dropped half, and `.stage .tag` carries the body.

@media (max-width:56rem) | .mascot-riso.why: Same ruling, the narrow breakpoint: the cap that keeps the fox inside its column at phone widths, which the snapshot's own rule does not express.

@media (max-width:64rem) | .hero-grid.why: The 64rem block ships the gap and NOT grid-template-columns:1fr. That declaration was dead in the snapshot - a later section overrode it - and moving the block into this sheet brought it to life, collapsing the hero to one column from 897 to 1024px. Dropped deliberately; #566's third round is the record.

.m-dir.why: THE MASCOT'S INNER DOM IS THE `page-mascot` PACKAGE'S, NOT OURS. The design draws the fox from its own markup and we render <Mascot/> from the package, which ships its own structure and styling. Transcribing these would be a second, competing description of a DOM we do not author, and the first time the package changed its internals ours would point at elements that no longer exist. The rendered result is checked by scripts/mascot-check.mjs instead of the rules behind it.

@media (max-width:32rem) | #lookupform ..why: A 44px TAP FLOOR THE DESIGN DOES NOT CARRY. The approved preview is a desktop mock and has no touch-target rule anywhere; shipping it as drawn puts 23-30px controls under a finger. SDE-App's #593 survey found NINE scoped floors across this codebase with THREE different triggers - (pointer:coarse), max-width:32rem and max-width:56rem - so a touch device at 1024px gets one answer and a narrow desktop window another. #593 replaces the scattered subjects AND unifies the trigger; these entries come out with it. Declared rather than dropped because a floor of ours the design cannot satisfy is exactly what an `override` is.
